questions.prompt: Which is a benefit of cloud computing?
choices: Trade variable expense for capital expense
questions.explanation: Elastic scaling means you no longer have to guess capacity up front.

questions.prompt: Which pillar of the Well-Architected Framework focuses on recovering from failures?
questions.explanation: Reliability covers recovering from failures and meeting demand.

questions.prompt: Running applications across multiple Availability Zones primarily improves:
questions.explanation: Multiple AZs protect against a single data-centre failure.

questions.prompt: Which describes an AWS Region?
choices: A geographic area with multiple isolated AZs
questions.explanation: A Region is a geographic area containing multiple Availability Zones.

questions.prompt: Under the shared responsibility model, who is responsible for physical security of data centres?
questions.explanation: AWS is responsible for security OF the cloud, including physical facilities.

questions.prompt: What is the best practice for the AWS account root user?
choices: Enable MFA and avoid everyday use
questions.explanation: Protect the root user with MFA and use IAM identities for daily tasks.

questions.prompt: Which service gives on-demand access to AWS compliance reports?
questions.explanation: AWS Artifact provides compliance reports such as SOC and ISO.

questions.prompt: Which service protects against DDoS attacks?
questions.explanation: AWS Shield (Standard is free) protects against DDoS.

questions.prompt: Which service detects threats by analysing CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs and DNS logs?
questions.explanation: GuardDuty is an intelligent threat detection service.

questions.prompt: Which service records API calls made in an AWS account?
questions.explanation: CloudTrail logs API activity for auditing.

questions.prompt: Which service provides resizable virtual servers?
questions.explanation: EC2 provides virtual machines (instances).

questions.prompt: Which service runs code without provisioning servers?
questions.explanation: Lambda is serverless compute billed per request and duration.

questions.prompt: Which storage service is object storage with very high durability?
questions.explanation: S3 is object storage designed for 11 nines of durability.

questions.prompt: Which service is a managed NoSQL key-value database?
questions.explanation: DynamoDB is a serverless NoSQL key-value and document database.

questions.prompt: Which service is a content delivery network?
questions.explanation: CloudFront caches content at edge locations worldwide.

questions.prompt: Which service provides a dedicated private network connection from on-premises to AWS?
questions.explanation: Direct Connect is a dedicated private link that doesn't traverse the internet.

questions.prompt: Which service is AWS's DNS service?
questions.explanation: Amazon Route 53 provides DNS and domain registration.

questions.prompt: Which EC2 pricing option is best for interruptible, flexible workloads at the lowest cost?
questions.explanation: Spot Instances use spare capacity at large discounts but can be interrupted.

questions.prompt: Which tool helps forecast and visualise AWS spending over time?
questions.explanation: Cost Explorer visualises historical costs and forecasts.

questions.prompt: Which tool estimates costs BEFORE deploying an architecture?
questions.explanation: The Pricing Calculator estimates costs for planned workloads.

questions.prompt: Which support plan is the lowest tier that includes a designated Technical Account Manager?
questions.explanation: Enterprise On-Ramp gives access to a pool of TAMs; Enterprise gives a designated TAM. (Check current AWS docs, as plans change.)

questions.prompt: Which feature of AWS Organizations combines billing for multiple accounts?
questions.explanation: Consolidated billing gives one bill and volume discounts across accounts.

questions.prompt: A startup wants to avoid buying servers up front and pay only for the compute it actually uses. Which cloud benefit does this describe?
choices: Trade fixed capital expense for variable expense
Benefit from massive economies of scale
Stop spending money on data center cooling only
questions.explanation: Paying as you go replaces large up-front hardware purchases (CapEx) with variable operating expense (OpEx).

questions.prompt: Why can AWS often offer lower pay-as-you-go prices than a company could achieve on its own?
choices: Aggregated usage from many customers creates massive economies of scale
AWS requires multi-year contracts from every customer
Customers manage the physical hardware themselves
questions.explanation: Because AWS serves hundreds of thousands of customers, its scale lowers costs, which it passes on as lower prices.

questions.prompt: A retailer's traffic spikes during holidays and falls afterward. Which cloud characteristic lets it add and remove capacity automatically to match demand?
questions.explanation: Elasticity is the ability to acquire resources when needed and release them when no longer needed.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes 'go global in minutes' as a benefit of AWS?
choices: Applications can be deployed in multiple Regions worldwide with a few clicks
AWS automatically translates application interfaces into local languages
All AWS services are free in every country
Data is automatically replicated to every Region
questions.explanation: AWS's global infrastructure lets you deploy to Regions around the world quickly, reducing latency for global users.

questions.prompt: Which cloud deployment model runs all application parts in the cloud with no on-premises components?
questions.explanation: A cloud deployment runs all parts of the application in the cloud, either migrated or built there from the start.

questions.prompt: A company connects its on-premises data center to AWS and runs some workloads in each. Which deployment model is this?
questions.explanation: A hybrid deployment links cloud resources with existing on-premises infrastructure.

questions.prompt: Amazon EC2, where the customer manages the operating system and applications, is an example of which cloud computing model?
questions.explanation: IaaS provides virtual compute, storage and networking while the customer manages the OS and above.

questions.prompt: AWS Elastic Beanstalk lets developers upload code while AWS handles capacity provisioning, load balancing and patching of the platform. Which model best fits?
questions.explanation: PaaS removes the need to manage underlying infrastructure so teams can focus on deploying and managing applications.

questions.prompt: Which is an example of Software as a Service (SaaS)?
choices: A virtual machine you patch yourself
A complete hosted email application used through a web browser
A managed container runtime where you deploy code
A rack of servers in your data center
questions.explanation: SaaS delivers a finished product run and managed by the provider; users simply consume it.

questions.prompt: Which Well-Architected pillar focuses on minimizing the environmental impact of running cloud workloads?
questions.explanation: The Sustainability pillar covers reducing energy use and improving resource efficiency to lower environmental impact.

questions.prompt: Which Well-Architected pillar includes the design principle 'perform operations as code'?
questions.explanation: Operational Excellence emphasizes running and monitoring systems, including defining operations as code.

questions.prompt: A team wants to choose the right instance types and use serverless technologies so resources meet requirements as demand changes. Which Well-Architected pillar is this?
questions.explanation: Performance Efficiency is about using computing resources efficiently to meet requirements and maintaining that efficiency as demand changes.

questions.prompt: 'Apply security at all layers' and 'enable traceability' are design principles of which Well-Architected pillar?
questions.explanation: These principles belong to the Security pillar, which focuses on protecting data, systems and assets.

questions.prompt: Which Well-Architected pillar includes 'adopt a consumption model' and 'measure overall efficiency' as design principles?
questions.explanation: Cost Optimization focuses on avoiding unnecessary cost, including paying only for what you consume.

questions.prompt: Which free AWS tool lets you review a workload against Well-Architected best practices and track improvement items?
questions.explanation: The Well-Architected Tool in the console guides you through questions per pillar and records high- and medium-risk issues.

questions.prompt: How many pillars does the AWS Well-Architected Framework currently define?
questions.explanation: The six pillars are Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization and Sustainability.

questions.prompt: What is an AWS Availability Zone?
choices: A single server rack shared by many customers
A content delivery cache in a major city
One or more discrete data centers with redundant power, networking and connectivity within a Region
A logical grouping of AWS accounts
questions.explanation: Each AZ consists of one or more physically separate data centers, isolated from failures in other AZs.

questions.prompt: Which factor is usually the FIRST consideration when selecting an AWS Region for a workload holding regulated personal data?
choices: The number of edge locations in the Region
The Region's alphabetical position in the console
questions.explanation: Legal and regulatory requirements about where data must reside often rule Regions in or out before latency, service availability or price.

questions.prompt: Which three factors, besides compliance, commonly guide Region selection?
choices: Number of IAM users, VPC count and bucket names
Proximity to users, service availability and pricing
Support plan level, account age and root user email
Operating system, programming language and IDE
questions.explanation: Latency to customers, which services are offered in the Region, and Region-specific pricing all influence the choice.

questions.prompt: What are AWS edge locations primarily used for?
choices: Caching content closer to users for services such as CloudFront and Route 53
Running all EC2 instances for a Region
Storing the only copy of S3 data
questions.explanation: Edge locations serve cached content and DNS responses near users to reduce latency.

questions.prompt: A game company needs single-digit millisecond latency for players in a specific metropolitan area. Which infrastructure option places AWS compute closer to those users?
questions.explanation: Local Zones extend a Region by placing compute, storage and other services in large metro areas near end users.

questions.prompt: Which AWS infrastructure offering embeds compute and storage within 5G telecommunication networks for ultra-low latency to mobile devices?
questions.explanation: Wavelength Zones embed AWS services inside telecom providers' 5G networks.

questions.prompt: A company needs to run AWS services on premises in its own data center with the same APIs and tools as the cloud. Which offering fits?
questions.explanation: Outposts delivers AWS-managed infrastructure installed in the customer's facility for a consistent hybrid experience.

questions.prompt: Designing an application so that the failure of one component does not bring down the whole system describes which architectural concept?
questions.explanation: Loosely coupled components, for example connected through queues, reduce dependencies so one failure does not cascade.

questions.prompt: Adding more EC2 instances behind a load balancer rather than upgrading to a larger instance is called:
questions.explanation: Horizontal scaling (scaling out) adds more resources of the same type to share the load.

questions.prompt: Replacing a server with a larger instance type that has more CPU and memory is an example of:
questions.explanation: Vertical scaling (scaling up) increases the size of an individual resource.

questions.prompt: Which design principle suggests treating servers as disposable resources that can be replaced rather than repaired?
choices: Name servers individually and patch by hand
Keep a single large server for simplicity
questions.explanation: In the cloud, automated replacement of resources is faster and more consistent than repairing long-lived servers.

questions.prompt: Which of the six perspectives of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) focuses on ensuring cloud investments accelerate digital transformation and business outcomes?
questions.explanation: The Business perspective helps ensure cloud investments align with and accelerate business outcomes.

questions.prompt: Which AWS CAF perspective addresses culture, organizational structure, leadership and workforce skills during cloud adoption?
questions.explanation: The People perspective bridges technology and business, focusing on culture, change and talent.

questions.prompt: Which AWS CAF perspective focuses on orchestrating cloud initiatives while maximizing benefits and minimizing transformation risks, including program and portfolio management?
questions.explanation: The Governance perspective covers program and project management, benefits management, risk and financial management.

questions.prompt: Which AWS CAF perspective helps build an enterprise-grade, scalable hybrid cloud platform and modernize workloads?
questions.explanation: The Platform perspective covers platform architecture, engineering, data engineering and CI/CD.

questions.prompt: Which AWS CAF perspective ensures cloud services are delivered at an agreed level, including observability, incident and problem management?
questions.explanation: The Operations perspective focuses on running cloud services reliably to meet business needs.

questions.prompt: Which list correctly names the four transformation domains described in the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework?
questions.explanation: AWS CAF says value comes from transforming technology, process, organization and product.

questions.prompt: A company moves an application to EC2 with no code changes. Which migration strategy is this?
questions.explanation: Rehosting moves applications as-is to the cloud without modification.

questions.prompt: A company migrates its self-managed database to Amazon RDS to reduce administration, without changing the application's core architecture. Which migration strategy is this?
questions.explanation: Replatforming makes a few cloud optimizations, such as using a managed database, without re-architecting.

questions.prompt: Moving from an on-premises CRM to a SaaS CRM product is which migration strategy?
questions.explanation: Repurchasing means moving to a different product, often a SaaS offering.

questions.prompt: A company re-architects a monolith into microservices using AWS Lambda to add features and scale. Which migration strategy is this?
questions.explanation: Refactoring reimagines how the application is architected using cloud-native features.

questions.prompt: During migration planning, a team finds applications that are no longer used and decides to shut them down. Which strategy is this?
questions.explanation: Retiring removes applications that are no longer needed, reducing cost and attack surface.

questions.prompt: Which migration strategy describes keeping certain applications on premises for now, for example because they were recently upgraded?
questions.explanation: Retain means leaving applications in the source environment until migrating makes sense.

questions.prompt: Moving VMware-based workloads to VMware Cloud on AWS without buying new hardware or rewriting applications is an example of which strategy?
questions.explanation: Relocate moves infrastructure to the cloud at the hypervisor level without changing the applications.

questions.prompt: Which is a key benefit of the AWS Cloud regarding speed and agility?
choices: Procurement cycles are replaced by annual hardware refreshes
New IT resources are available in minutes, lowering the cost and time of experimentation
Developers must wait for capacity planning reviews
Every resource requires a signed purchase order
questions.explanation: Fast provisioning lets teams experiment and innovate quickly with little up-front cost.

questions.prompt: A company no longer wants staff spending time racking, stacking and powering servers. Which cloud benefit addresses this?
choices: Increase speed of data replication between disks
Gain physical access to AWS hardware
Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers
questions.explanation: AWS handles the physical infrastructure, freeing teams to focus on projects that differentiate the business.

questions.prompt: Which concept describes AWS infrastructure being shared securely among many customers with logical isolation?
questions.explanation: Cloud resources are pooled across customers, with isolation enforced logically by the provider.

questions.prompt: Why is deploying an application across multiple AWS Regions useful beyond multi-AZ deployments?
choices: It is required for all AWS workloads
It removes the need for backups
It makes data transfer between Regions free
It protects against a Region-wide disruption and can reduce latency for users in other geographies
questions.explanation: Multi-Region designs add geographic resilience and can serve global users from nearby locations.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the total cost of ownership (TCO) of moving to the cloud is accurate?
choices: TCO only compares server purchase prices
TCO includes indirect costs such as facilities, power, cooling and staff time, not just server prices
TCO is always higher in the cloud
questions.explanation: A full TCO comparison accounts for data center, hardware, software, labor and operational overheads.

questions.prompt: Rightsizing in the cloud means:
choices: Always choosing the largest instance available
Matching instance types and sizes to actual workload performance and capacity needs
Buying hardware sized for five years of growth
Moving every workload to a single Region
questions.explanation: Rightsizing removes over-provisioning so you pay only for capacity you actually need.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes high availability in AWS?
choices: All data is stored on one very large server
Applications run only during business hours
Systems keep running with minimal downtime by removing single points of failure, for example using multiple AZs
questions.explanation: High availability designs use redundancy across isolated infrastructure so failures cause little or no downtime.

questions.prompt: Which practice is part of the Sustainability pillar's guidance?
choices: Keep idle servers running in case they are needed
Choose Regions only by alphabetical order
Duplicate all data to every Region by default
Maximize utilization so fewer, more efficiently used resources do the same work
questions.explanation: Higher utilization and removing idle resources reduce energy consumed per unit of work.

questions.prompt: Under the shared responsibility model, which task is the customer's responsibility when using Amazon EC2?
questions.explanation: With EC2 (IaaS), customers manage the guest OS, including updates and security patches.

questions.prompt: When using Amazon RDS, who is responsible for patching the database engine software?
choices: The customer must patch it manually by logging into the host
AWS, within the maintenance window the customer configures
Nobody; RDS engines are never patched
questions.explanation: RDS is a managed service, so AWS applies OS and engine patches while customers control timing and settings.

questions.prompt: Which responsibility is shared between AWS and the customer under the shared responsibility model?
questions.explanation: Patch management, configuration management and awareness and training are shared controls: AWS patches its infrastructure, customers patch their systems.

questions.prompt: Under the shared responsibility model, which item is ALWAYS the customer's responsibility regardless of the service used?
choices: Customer data and who is granted access to it
questions.explanation: Customers always own their data, its classification and access management, even with fully managed services.

questions.prompt: For AWS Lambda, which security task remains the customer's responsibility?
choices: Patching the underlying execution environment OS
Securing the function code and its IAM permissions
questions.explanation: AWS manages the Lambda runtime infrastructure; customers are responsible for their code, configuration and permissions.

questions.prompt: Configuring security groups on EC2 instances is the responsibility of:
questions.explanation: Security groups are customer-configured virtual firewalls, part of security in the cloud.

questions.prompt: What does the phrase 'security OF the cloud' refer to?
choices: AWS protecting the infrastructure that runs all AWS services
questions.explanation: AWS is responsible for security of the cloud: hardware, software, networking and facilities.

questions.prompt: Which IAM best practice grants users only the permissions needed to perform their tasks?
choices: Full administrator access for all developers
Permission inheritance from the root user
questions.explanation: Least privilege reduces risk by limiting permissions to what each identity actually needs.

questions.prompt: An application on an EC2 instance needs to read from an S3 bucket. What is the most secure way to grant access?
choices: Store an IAM user's access keys in the application's configuration file
Use the root user's access keys
Attach an IAM role to the instance with a policy allowing the required S3 actions
questions.explanation: IAM roles provide temporary credentials automatically, avoiding long-term keys stored on the instance.

questions.prompt: What is an IAM group used for?
choices: Attaching permissions to a collection of IAM users so they share the same access
Grouping EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group
Combining multiple AWS accounts for billing
Signing in to the console as a team
questions.explanation: Groups simplify permission management; users in a group inherit the group's policies. Groups cannot sign in themselves.

questions.prompt: Which format are IAM policies written in?
questions.explanation: IAM policy documents are JSON statements with Effect, Action, Resource and optional Condition elements.

questions.prompt: If an IAM policy explicitly denies an action that another attached policy allows, what is the result?
choices: The most recently attached policy wins
The user is prompted to choose
questions.explanation: In IAM policy evaluation, an explicit deny always overrides any allow.

questions.prompt: Which task can be performed ONLY by the AWS account root user?
questions.explanation: A small set of tasks require the root user, such as closing the account, changing the root email or account name, and restoring IAM user permissions; everyday tasks like launching instances or creating buckets should be done with IAM identities.

questions.prompt: Which service provides a central place for workforce users to sign in once and access multiple AWS accounts and business applications?
questions.explanation: IAM Identity Center (successor to AWS SSO) provides single sign-on across AWS accounts and applications.

questions.prompt: A mobile app needs user sign-up, sign-in and social identity provider login for its customers. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: Cognito provides customer identity and access management for web and mobile apps.

questions.prompt: Which AWS Organizations feature sets the maximum permissions available to accounts in an organizational unit?
questions.explanation: SCPs act as guardrails that limit the permissions IAM identities in member accounts can use.

questions.prompt: Which service helps set up and govern a secure multi-account AWS environment using pre-configured guardrails?
questions.explanation: Control Tower automates a landing zone with best-practice accounts and preventive and detective controls.

questions.prompt: Which IAM feature requires users to provide a second factor, such as a code from a device, in addition to a password?
questions.explanation: MFA adds a second authentication factor, greatly reducing the risk from stolen passwords.

questions.prompt: Which tool identifies resources, such as S3 buckets or IAM roles, that are shared with an external entity?
questions.explanation: IAM Access Analyzer uses logic-based reasoning to find resource policies that grant access outside your zone of trust.

questions.prompt: Which report lists IAM users and the status of their credentials, such as passwords, access keys and MFA devices?
questions.explanation: The credential report helps audit credential lifecycle and MFA use across an account.

questions.prompt: Which service creates and controls cryptographic keys used to encrypt data across AWS services?
questions.explanation: KMS manages encryption keys and integrates with many AWS services for data-at-rest encryption.

questions.prompt: A company must store encryption keys in dedicated, single-tenant hardware security modules that it controls. Which service fits?
choices: AWS KMS with AWS managed keys
questions.explanation: CloudHSM provides dedicated FIPS-validated HSMs in your VPC under your exclusive control.

questions.prompt: Which service provisions and automatically renews public SSL/TLS certificates for use with Elastic Load Balancing and CloudFront?
questions.explanation: ACM issues and renews certificates and deploys them to integrated services such as ELB and CloudFront.

questions.prompt: An application needs to store a database password and rotate it automatically on a schedule. Which service is designed for this?
questions.explanation: Secrets Manager stores secrets securely and can rotate them automatically, including for RDS credentials.

questions.prompt: Encrypting data while it moves between a client and a web server, such as with TLS, protects data:
questions.explanation: TLS encryption protects data in transit across networks.

questions.prompt: Which service uses machine learning to discover and protect sensitive data such as personally identifiable information in Amazon S3?
questions.explanation: Macie automatically discovers, classifies and reports sensitive data stored in S3.

questions.prompt: Which service automatically scans EC2 instances, container images in Amazon ECR and Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure?
questions.explanation: Inspector continuously scans workloads for known CVEs and network reachability issues.

questions.prompt: A security team wants to filter HTTP requests to an Application Load Balancer, blocking SQL injection and cross-site scripting attempts. Which service should they use?
questions.explanation: AWS WAF is a web application firewall that inspects layer 7 requests against rules such as SQLi and XSS protections.

questions.prompt: Which statement about AWS Shield Standard is correct?
choices: It must be purchased with a one-year commitment
It includes 24/7 access to the Shield Response Team
It is automatically enabled for all AWS customers at no additional cost
questions.explanation: Shield Standard protects against common network and transport layer DDoS attacks for every customer by default.

questions.prompt: Which benefit is included with AWS Shield Advanced but NOT Shield Standard?
choices: Access to the AWS Shield Response Team and DDoS cost protection
Free AWS WAF for any account without subscription
questions.explanation: Shield Advanced adds enhanced detection, 24/7 SRT support and protection against scaling charges caused by DDoS attacks.

questions.prompt: Which service aggregates and prioritizes security findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie and partner tools, and runs automated best-practice checks?
questions.explanation: Security Hub provides a consolidated view of security alerts and posture checks against standards such as AWS Foundational Security Best Practices.

questions.prompt: After GuardDuty raises a finding, an analyst wants to visualize related activity and investigate the root cause. Which service helps most?
questions.explanation: Detective builds behavior graphs from log data to help investigate security findings.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Amazon GuardDuty is accurate?
choices: It is a firewall that blocks traffic at the edge
It scans application source code for bugs
It analyzes data sources continuously without requiring agents to be installed for its core log analysis
questions.explanation: GuardDuty is a managed threat detection service that analyzes logs such as CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs and DNS logs.

questions.prompt: Which service continuously records resource configuration changes and evaluates them against rules, such as 'S3 buckets must have encryption enabled'?
questions.explanation: AWS Config tracks configuration history and assesses compliance with Config rules.

questions.prompt: An auditor asks who deleted a security group yesterday. Which service provides that information?
questions.explanation: CloudTrail logs API calls including the identity, time, source IP and parameters of the request.

questions.prompt: Which service helps continuously collect evidence and audit AWS usage to simplify assessments against standards and regulations?
questions.explanation: Audit Manager automates evidence collection and maps it to compliance frameworks.

questions.prompt: Which service lets you review and accept agreements such as the Business Associate Addendum (BAA) with AWS?
questions.explanation: Artifact provides compliance reports and lets you manage agreements such as the BAA.

questions.prompt: Which VPC feature is a stateful firewall applied at the instance (elastic network interface) level?
questions.explanation: Security groups are stateful: return traffic is automatically allowed, and they support allow rules only.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes a network ACL?
choices: It is a stateless firewall at the subnet level that supports both allow and deny rules
It is a stateful firewall attached to an instance
questions.explanation: Network ACLs evaluate inbound and outbound traffic separately for a subnet and can explicitly deny traffic.

questions.prompt: A company wants to block traffic from a specific malicious IP address range at the subnet level. Which feature should it use?
questions.explanation: Security groups cannot contain deny rules; network ACLs can deny specific IP ranges.

questions.prompt: Which managed service centrally configures and manages firewall rules, such as AWS WAF rules and security group policies, across accounts in AWS Organizations?
questions.explanation: Firewall Manager applies security policies consistently across accounts and resources.

questions.prompt: Which AWS service provides a managed, stateful network firewall and intrusion prevention for traffic in a VPC?
questions.explanation: Network Firewall deploys managed firewall endpoints with stateful inspection and IPS rules in VPCs.

questions.prompt: Who is permitted to perform penetration testing on certain AWS services, such as EC2, without prior approval?
choices: AWS customers, on their own resources and for the permitted services
Any third party against any AWS customer
questions.explanation: AWS allows customers to pentest their own resources on listed services without approval, subject to AWS policy.

questions.prompt: What should a customer do if they suspect AWS resources are being used for abusive activity such as spam or DDoS attacks?
choices: Report it to the AWS Trust & Safety team
Post it in AWS re:Post only
questions.explanation: The AWS Trust & Safety team handles abuse reports involving AWS resources.

questions.prompt: Which statement about encryption of Amazon S3 objects is correct?
choices: S3 objects can never be encrypted
New objects are encrypted at rest by default with S3 managed keys
Only Glacier storage classes support encryption
questions.explanation: S3 applies server-side encryption with S3 managed keys (SSE-S3) to all new objects by default.

questions.prompt: Which S3 feature can prevent objects from being deleted or overwritten for a fixed period, supporting write-once-read-many (WORM) requirements?
questions.explanation: Object Lock enforces retention periods or legal holds so objects cannot be changed or deleted.

questions.prompt: Which setting helps prevent accidental public exposure of S3 buckets across an entire account?
questions.explanation: Block Public Access settings override policies and ACLs that would grant public access.

questions.prompt: Which program provides details on how AWS meets compliance standards such as ISO 27001, PCI DSS and SOC 2?
choices: AWS compliance programs with reports available in AWS Artifact
questions.explanation: AWS participates in many assurance programs, and customers download the related reports from Artifact.

questions.prompt: A company is responsible for complying with regulations for its workload on AWS. Which statement is accurate?
choices: AWS compliance certifications cover the infrastructure, but the customer must still make its own workload compliant
AWS certifications automatically make every customer workload compliant
Compliance applies only to on-premises systems
questions.explanation: Under shared responsibility, customers inherit infrastructure controls but must configure their applications and data to meet requirements.

questions.prompt: Which AWS service lets you store, audit and manage the lifecycle of encryption keys and logs every key use in CloudTrail?
questions.explanation: KMS integrates with CloudTrail so every use of a key can be audited.

questions.prompt: Which feature of Amazon VPC captures information about IP traffic going to and from network interfaces?
questions.explanation: Flow Logs record accepted and rejected traffic metadata for troubleshooting and security analysis.

questions.prompt: A company wants AWS to automatically block requests from countries it does not serve before they reach its CloudFront distribution. Which service can apply this geographic rule?
questions.explanation: AWS WAF rules can match the country of origin of requests and block them at CloudFront or other protected resources.

questions.prompt: Which AWS service provides a centralized security data lake by normalizing security logs into the Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF)?
questions.explanation: Security Lake centralizes security data from AWS, SaaS and on-premises sources in OCSF format.

questions.prompt: A developer accidentally committed IAM access keys to a public repository. What should be done FIRST?
choices: Deactivate and delete the exposed access keys, then create new ones if needed
Delete the repository and take no other action
questions.explanation: Exposed long-term credentials must be revoked immediately to stop misuse.

questions.prompt: Which type of IAM identity provides temporary credentials and can be assumed by users, applications or AWS services?
questions.explanation: Roles have no long-term credentials; principals assume them to receive temporary security credentials.

questions.prompt: Which feature lets you require that an IAM user's password meet complexity rules and be rotated periodically?
questions.explanation: IAM password policies set requirements such as minimum length, character types and expiration.

questions.prompt: Which type of policy is attached directly to a resource, such as an S3 bucket, to specify who can access it?
questions.explanation: Resource-based policies are attached to resources and specify which principals can perform actions on them.

questions.prompt: Which AWS offering lets customers deploy security solutions from third-party vendors, such as firewalls and endpoint protection, often billed through their AWS account?
questions.explanation: AWS Marketplace is a curated catalog of third-party software, including security products.

questions.prompt: Which service helps you quickly assess, monitor and improve the security posture of your Amazon EKS or ECS container workloads by detecting runtime threats?
questions.explanation: GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring detects threats such as suspicious processes in EKS, ECS and EC2 workloads.

questions.prompt: Which concept describes encrypting data with a data key and then encrypting that data key with a KMS key?
questions.explanation: Envelope encryption protects data keys with a master (KMS) key, improving performance and key management.

questions.prompt: Which EC2 instance family is optimized for memory-intensive workloads such as in-memory databases?
questions.explanation: Memory optimized instances provide high memory-to-CPU ratios for large in-memory datasets.

questions.prompt: A batch job performs high-performance scientific modeling that needs many fast CPU cores. Which EC2 instance family is most suitable?
questions.explanation: Compute optimized instances suit compute-bound workloads like HPC, batch processing and scientific modeling.

questions.prompt: Which EC2 instance category uses hardware accelerators such as GPUs for machine learning training?
questions.explanation: Accelerated computing instances include GPUs or custom chips like AWS Trainium and Inferentia.

questions.prompt: Which service automatically adds or removes EC2 instances based on demand or a schedule?
questions.explanation: EC2 Auto Scaling maintains the desired capacity and scales based on policies or schedules.

questions.prompt: Which Elastic Load Balancing type operates at layer 7 and can route requests based on URL path or host header?
questions.explanation: ALB supports content-based routing for HTTP and HTTPS traffic.

questions.prompt: An application needs to handle millions of TCP requests per second with ultra-low latency and static IP addresses. Which load balancer fits best?
questions.explanation: NLB operates at layer 4, offering very high throughput, low latency and static IPs per AZ.

questions.prompt: Which service offers simple virtual private servers with bundled storage, networking and predictable monthly pricing, ideal for small websites?
questions.explanation: Lightsail provides easy-to-use VPS bundles for simple workloads.

questions.prompt: Which AWS service runs Docker containers without requiring you to manage servers or clusters of EC2 instances?
questions.explanation: Fargate is a serverless compute engine for containers used with ECS and EKS.

questions.prompt: Which service is a managed Kubernetes control plane on AWS?
questions.explanation: EKS runs and scales the Kubernetes control plane for you.

questions.prompt: Where can developers store, manage and share Docker container images in AWS?
questions.explanation: ECR is a fully managed container image registry integrated with ECS, EKS and Lambda.

questions.prompt: Which service plans, schedules and runs batch computing workloads across EC2 and Fargate?
questions.explanation: AWS Batch dynamically provisions compute resources based on the volume and requirements of batch jobs.

questions.prompt: A developer wants to deploy a containerized web application from source code or an image with automatic scaling and no infrastructure configuration. Which service is simplest?
questions.explanation: App Runner builds and runs web apps and APIs from code or container images with minimal setup.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum execution duration of a single AWS Lambda function invocation?
questions.explanation: Lambda functions can run for up to 900 seconds per invocation.

questions.prompt: Which storage type is block storage that can be attached to a single EC2 instance in the same Availability Zone, persisting independently of the instance's life?
questions.explanation: EBS volumes are network-attached block storage that persist after the instance stops and are AZ-scoped.

questions.prompt: Which statement about EC2 instance store volumes is correct?
choices: Data is automatically replicated across Regions
They are the same as EBS snapshots
Data is lost when the instance is stopped or terminated
They can be detached and attached to other instances
questions.explanation: Instance store provides temporary block storage physically attached to the host; it is ephemeral.

questions.prompt: Several Linux EC2 instances across multiple AZs need to share a file system that grows and shrinks automatically. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: EFS is a managed, elastic NFS file system that many instances can mount concurrently.

questions.prompt: A company needs a fully managed Windows-native file system accessible over SMB that integrates with Microsoft Active Directory. Which service fits?
choices: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
questions.explanation: FSx for Windows File Server provides SMB shares with AD integration.

questions.prompt: Which service provides a high-performance file system for compute-intensive workloads like HPC and machine learning, and can link to S3?
choices: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
questions.explanation: FSx for Lustre offers sub-millisecond latency and high throughput and integrates with S3.

questions.prompt: Which S3 storage class automatically moves objects between access tiers when access patterns change, without retrieval fees?
questions.explanation: Intelligent-Tiering monitors access and moves objects to the most cost-effective tier automatically.

questions.prompt: Which S3 storage class is the lowest-cost option for data retained for years and accessed rarely, with retrieval times of hours?
questions.explanation: Deep Archive is the cheapest S3 class, designed for long-term retention with retrieval within about 12 to 48 hours.

questions.prompt: Which S3 storage class stores data in a single Availability Zone at lower cost, suitable for easily re-creatable, infrequently accessed data?
questions.explanation: One Zone-IA costs less because it does not replicate across multiple AZs.

questions.prompt: Which S3 feature automatically transitions objects to cheaper storage classes or deletes them after a defined period?
questions.explanation: Lifecycle rules define transitions and expirations based on object age.

questions.prompt: Which S3 feature keeps multiple variants of an object so you can recover from accidental overwrites or deletions?
questions.explanation: Versioning preserves every version of every object in a bucket.

questions.prompt: Which service connects on-premises applications to AWS cloud storage using file, volume or tape interfaces?
questions.explanation: Storage Gateway is a hybrid storage service offering file, volume and tape gateways.

questions.prompt: Which service centrally manages and automates backups across services such as EBS, RDS, DynamoDB and EFS?
questions.explanation: AWS Backup provides policy-based backup plans across many AWS services.

questions.prompt: Which managed relational database engine, built by AWS, is compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL and offers higher performance than standard engines?
questions.explanation: Aurora is a cloud-native relational database compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL.

questions.prompt: Which Amazon RDS feature creates a synchronous standby copy of the database in another AZ for automatic failover?
questions.explanation: Multi-AZ provides high availability by synchronously replicating to a standby in a different AZ.

questions.prompt: A read-heavy application wants to offload read traffic from its primary RDS database. What should it use?
questions.explanation: Read replicas use asynchronous replication to serve read queries and scale read capacity.

questions.prompt: Which service is a fully managed in-memory caching service compatible with Redis OSS, Valkey or Memcached?
questions.explanation: ElastiCache provides in-memory caches that reduce database load and latency.

questions.prompt: Which feature adds a microsecond-latency in-memory cache specifically for Amazon DynamoDB?
questions.explanation: DAX is a fully managed, DynamoDB-compatible in-memory cache.

questions.prompt: A social network needs to store and query highly connected relationship data such as friends of friends. Which database is purpose-built for this?
questions.explanation: Neptune is a managed graph database optimized for relationships.

questions.prompt: Which service is a managed document database compatible with MongoDB workloads?
questions.explanation: DocumentDB stores, queries and indexes JSON data with MongoDB compatibility.

questions.prompt: An IoT application needs to store and analyze trillions of time-stamped sensor readings. Which database is purpose-built for this?
questions.explanation: Timestream is a time series database optimized for IoT and operational metrics.

questions.prompt: Which service is a petabyte-scale data warehouse for running complex analytic SQL queries?
questions.explanation: Redshift is a columnar, managed data warehouse for analytics.

questions.prompt: Which service lets analysts run standard SQL queries directly against data in Amazon S3 without loading it or managing servers?
questions.explanation: Athena is a serverless interactive query service that bills per data scanned.

questions.prompt: Which service is a serverless data integration (ETL) service with a Data Catalog for discovering data?
questions.explanation: Glue crawls data sources, builds a catalog and runs ETL jobs without servers.

questions.prompt: Which service provides managed big data frameworks such as Apache Spark and Hadoop?
questions.explanation: EMR runs open-source big data frameworks on managed clusters or serverless.

questions.prompt: Which service creates interactive business intelligence dashboards and visualizations?
questions.explanation: QuickSight is a cloud-scale BI service for dashboards and reports.

questions.prompt: A company needs to collect and process clickstream data in real time from thousands of sources. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: Kinesis Data Streams captures and stores real-time streaming data for processing.

questions.prompt: Which service delivers streaming data to destinations such as S3, Redshift and OpenSearch with no code required?
questions.explanation: Amazon Data Firehose (formerly Kinesis Data Firehose) loads streaming data into data stores and analytics tools.

questions.prompt: Which service is a managed search and log analytics engine, derived from Elasticsearch?
questions.explanation: OpenSearch Service runs OpenSearch clusters for search, log analytics and observability.

questions.prompt: Which service provides a fully managed message queue to decouple application components?
questions.explanation: SQS stores messages until consumers process them, decoupling producers from consumers.

questions.prompt: Which service uses a publish/subscribe model to push notifications to multiple subscribers such as email, SMS and SQS queues?
questions.explanation: SNS fans out messages from topics to many subscribers.

questions.prompt: Which serverless event bus routes events from AWS services, SaaS applications and custom apps to targets using rules?
questions.explanation: EventBridge is a serverless event bus that matches events to targets with rules.

questions.prompt: Which service coordinates multiple AWS services into serverless workflows using a visual state machine?
questions.explanation: Step Functions orchestrates steps, retries and branching between services.

questions.prompt: Which service lets you create, publish and secure REST and WebSocket APIs at any scale?
questions.explanation: API Gateway is a managed service for creating and managing APIs.

questions.prompt: Which VPC component allows resources in a public subnet to communicate with the internet?
questions.explanation: An internet gateway attached to a VPC, plus a route, enables internet access for public subnets.

questions.prompt: Instances in a private subnet need to download software updates from the internet without accepting inbound connections. What should be used?
choices: Internet gateway attached to the private subnet
questions.explanation: A NAT gateway lets private instances initiate outbound internet traffic while blocking unsolicited inbound traffic.

questions.prompt: Which service creates encrypted IPsec tunnels over the internet between an on-premises network and a VPC?
questions.explanation: Site-to-Site VPN provides encrypted connectivity over the public internet, quick to set up.

questions.prompt: A company has dozens of VPCs and on-premises networks and wants a central hub to interconnect them. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: Transit Gateway acts as a regional hub connecting VPCs and on-premises networks, simplifying routing.

questions.prompt: Which feature allows private connectivity from a VPC to services such as S3 or DynamoDB without traversing the internet?
questions.explanation: Gateway and interface VPC endpoints keep traffic to supported services on the AWS network.

questions.prompt: Which service improves availability and performance of global applications by routing users over the AWS global network using static anycast IP addresses?
questions.explanation: Global Accelerator provides two static anycast IPs and routes traffic to the optimal healthy endpoint.

questions.prompt: Which Route 53 routing policy sends users to the Region that gives them the lowest network latency?
questions.explanation: Latency routing directs users to the resource with the lowest measured latency.

questions.prompt: Which service lets you model and provision AWS infrastructure using templates written in JSON or YAML?
questions.explanation: CloudFormation provisions resources as stacks from infrastructure-as-code templates.

questions.prompt: Which tool lets developers define AWS infrastructure using familiar programming languages such as TypeScript or Python?
questions.explanation: The CDK synthesizes code into CloudFormation templates.

questions.prompt: Which service provides operational tools to patch, run commands on and manage fleets of EC2 and on-premises servers?
questions.explanation: Systems Manager includes Patch Manager, Run Command, Session Manager and Parameter Store.

questions.prompt: Which service collects metrics and logs and lets you set alarms on AWS resources?
questions.explanation: CloudWatch monitors resources and applications with metrics, logs, dashboards and alarms.

questions.prompt: Which service helps developers trace requests through distributed applications to find performance bottlenecks?
questions.explanation: X-Ray provides end-to-end tracing and service maps for applications.

questions.prompt: Which service gives a personalized view of AWS service events that may affect your specific resources?
questions.explanation: The AWS Health Dashboard shows account-specific events and scheduled changes.

questions.prompt: Which tool tracks the progress of application migrations across multiple AWS and partner tools in one place?
questions.explanation: Migration Hub provides a single location to track migration status.

questions.prompt: Which service migrates databases to AWS while the source database stays operational, supporting both homogeneous and heterogeneous migrations?
questions.explanation: DMS replicates data continuously so the source remains available, and works with the Schema Conversion Tool for different engines.

questions.prompt: Which service performs automated lift-and-shift migration of physical, virtual and cloud servers to AWS with minimal downtime?
questions.explanation: Application Migration Service continuously replicates source servers and launches them on EC2.

questions.prompt: A company must transfer 80 TB of data from a remote site with limited bandwidth. Which option is most practical?
choices: Uploading over the existing internet link
questions.explanation: Snowball Edge is a rugged physical device for transferring tens of terabytes offline, and also offers edge compute.

questions.prompt: Which service automates online data transfer between on-premises storage (such as NFS or SMB) and AWS storage services?
questions.explanation: DataSync moves data over the network quickly with automation, encryption and validation.

questions.prompt: Which service lets developers build, train and deploy custom machine learning models at scale?
questions.explanation: SageMaker AI provides tools across the full ML lifecycle for building, training and deploying models.

questions.prompt: Which service provides access to foundation models from Amazon and leading AI companies through a single API to build generative AI applications?
questions.explanation: Bedrock is a managed service offering foundation models via API without managing infrastructure.

questions.prompt: A company wants to automatically extract text, forms and tables from scanned documents. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: Textract uses ML to extract printed and handwritten text and structured data from documents.

questions.prompt: Which service converts text into lifelike speech?
questions.explanation: Polly is a text-to-speech service; Transcribe does the reverse.

questions.prompt: A company runs a steady database server 24/7 and will keep it for three years on the same instance type in one Region. Which pricing option gives significant savings with that commitment?
choices: EC2 Reserved Instances (or an EC2 Instance Savings Plan)
questions.explanation: Committing to steady usage for one or three years provides large discounts compared with On-Demand.

questions.prompt: Which Savings Plan type applies automatically to EC2, AWS Fargate and AWS Lambda usage regardless of instance family or Region?
questions.explanation: Compute Savings Plans offer the most flexibility, applying across instance families, Regions, OS, Fargate and Lambda.

questions.prompt: What does a customer commit to when purchasing a Savings Plan?
choices: A consistent amount of usage measured in dollars per hour for a one- or three-year term
A fixed number of EC2 instances for one month
A minimum number of IAM users
A fixed amount of S3 storage per year
questions.explanation: Savings Plans trade an hourly spend commitment for lower prices.

questions.prompt: A developer is testing a short-lived workload with unpredictable usage that cannot be interrupted. Which EC2 pricing option is most appropriate?
choices: Dedicated Hosts with a three-year reservation
questions.explanation: On-Demand has no commitment and is not interrupted, ideal for short-term, unpredictable workloads.

questions.prompt: Which EC2 option lets a company use existing server-bound software licenses, such as per-socket licenses, on physical servers dedicated to it?
questions.explanation: Dedicated Hosts give visibility into sockets and cores, supporting bring-your-own-license scenarios.

questions.prompt: Which statement about AWS data transfer pricing is generally true?
choices: Inbound data transfer from the internet into AWS is free, while outbound data transfer to the internet is charged
Inbound data is charged but outbound is free
Data transfer is charged only within an AZ
questions.explanation: AWS typically does not charge for data in, but charges for data out to the internet and some inter-Region and inter-AZ traffic.

questions.prompt: Which tool lets a company set a custom cost or usage threshold and receive alerts when actual or forecasted spending exceeds it?
questions.explanation: AWS Budgets sends alerts based on actual or forecasted cost and usage, and can trigger actions.

questions.prompt: Which source provides the most detailed, line-item billing data, delivered to an S3 bucket for analysis in tools like Athena?
questions.explanation: The CUR contains the most comprehensive cost and usage data, including hourly line items and resource IDs.

questions.prompt: What are cost allocation tags used for?
choices: Organizing and tracking AWS costs by labels such as project or department in billing reports
questions.explanation: Activated cost allocation tags appear in Cost Explorer and the CUR so costs can be grouped by tag.

questions.prompt: Which service uses machine learning to detect unusual spikes in AWS spending and alert you?
questions.explanation: Cost Anomaly Detection monitors spending patterns and notifies you of anomalies with root cause analysis.

questions.prompt: With consolidated billing in AWS Organizations, how are volume pricing tiers applied?
choices: Each account is billed separately at the highest tier
Usage across all member accounts is combined, so the organization may reach lower tier prices sooner
Only the management account's usage counts
questions.explanation: Consolidated billing aggregates usage, allowing tiered discounts and Reserved Instance or Savings Plan sharing across accounts.

questions.prompt: Which support plan is the lowest-cost plan that provides 24/7 access to Cloud Support Engineers by phone, chat and email?
questions.explanation: Business is the first tier with 24/7 technical support via phone, chat and email; Developer offers business-hours email access.

questions.prompt: Which capability is included with the AWS Basic Support plan at no cost?
choices: Access to AWS re:Post, documentation, the AWS Health Dashboard and core Trusted Advisor checks
24/7 phone support with Cloud Support Engineers
questions.explanation: Basic Support includes customer service, documentation, community forums and a limited set of Trusted Advisor checks.

questions.prompt: Which AWS support plan level is the first to include access to the full set of AWS Trusted Advisor checks?
choices: There is no plan that includes them
questions.explanation: Business, Enterprise On-Ramp and Enterprise Support include all Trusted Advisor checks.

questions.prompt: Which AWS Trusted Advisor category would identify idle EC2 instances and underutilized EBS volumes?
questions.explanation: Trusted Advisor's cost optimization checks flag resources you may be paying for but not using.

questions.prompt: Which team, available to Enterprise Support customers, offers proactive guidance and helps coordinate access to programs and experts?
choices: Technical Account Manager (TAM) and the Concierge Support Team
questions.explanation: Enterprise Support includes a designated TAM and a Concierge team for billing and account assistance.

questions.prompt: Which AWS program helps customers find consulting partners and software vendors that are validated for specific AWS competencies?
questions.explanation: The APN includes consulting and technology partners, and customers can find validated partners through the AWS Partner Solutions Finder.

questions.prompt: Which AWS offering lets customers try many services free within certain usage limits, including always-free offers and short-term trials?
questions.explanation: The Free Tier includes always-free offers, free trials and limited free usage for new accounts.

questions.prompt: Which EC2 pricing model can be up to 90% cheaper than On-Demand but can be interrupted by AWS with a two-minute warning?
questions.explanation: Spot Instances use spare capacity at steep discounts, but AWS can reclaim them with a two-minute interruption notice.

questions.prompt: A company wants to reserve EC2 capacity in a specific Availability Zone for a short planned event without a long-term commitment. Which option fits?
questions.explanation: On-Demand Capacity Reservations guarantee capacity in an AZ for any duration and can be cancelled anytime.

questions.prompt: Which AWS service lets you manage charges and pricing for internal teams or end customers by creating custom billing groups and rates?
questions.explanation: Billing Conductor creates pro forma billing data with custom pricing for showback and chargeback.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Reserved Instances is accurate?
choices: Standard Reserved Instances can be changed to any instance family at any time
Convertible Reserved Instances let you change instance family and OS, with a lower discount than Standard Reserved Instances
Reserved Instances are cheaper when bought for one month
Reserved Instances cannot be shared across accounts in an organization
questions.explanation: Convertible RIs trade some discount for flexibility to exchange for different instance attributes.

questions.prompt: Which Enterprise Support capability helps plan and run large events such as product launches or migrations with AWS experts?
questions.explanation: Infrastructure Event Management provides architecture and scaling guidance for planned high-traffic events.

questions.prompt: Which free AWS service gives recommendations to rightsize EC2 instances, EBS volumes and Lambda functions based on utilization metrics?
questions.explanation: Compute Optimizer uses machine learning on usage metrics to recommend optimal resource configurations.

questions.prompt: A startup wants to test a new product idea quickly and shut everything down at no further cost if it fails. Which cloud benefit is MOST relevant?
choices: Low cost of experimentation through on-demand resources
Lower latency through owning physical data center space
Guaranteed performance from dedicated single-tenant hardware
Fixed long-term pricing for all resources
questions.explanation: On-demand, pay-as-you-go resources let teams experiment cheaply and release resources when done, which increases agility.

questions.prompt: What is the key difference between scalability and elasticity?
choices: Scalability handles growth; elasticity matches resources to demand automatically
Elasticity requires buying hardware in advance, while scalability never requires it
Scalability applies only to storage, while elasticity applies only to compute resources
Scalability is always automatic, while elasticity always requires manual intervention
questions.explanation: Scalability is the ability to grow to handle more load, while elasticity adds and removes resources automatically as demand changes.

questions.prompt: Which is an example of a capital expenditure (CapEx) in IT?
choices: Paying an hourly rate for a running Amazon RDS instance
Buying physical servers for a company-owned data center
Paying a monthly bill for the Amazon EC2 instances a team uses
Paying per request for AWS Lambda function invocations
questions.explanation: CapEx is an up-front investment in physical assets such as servers; usage-based AWS charges are operational expenses.

questions.prompt: A finance team notices its AWS charges are recorded as monthly operating costs that vary with usage. Which financial model does this reflect?
questions.explanation: Pay-as-you-go cloud spending is a variable operational expense rather than an up-front capital investment.

questions.prompt: 'Test recovery procedures' and 'scale horizontally to increase aggregate workload availability' are design principles of which Well-Architected pillar?
questions.explanation: These principles belong to the Reliability pillar, which focuses on a workload performing its intended function correctly and consistently.

questions.prompt: Which Well-Architected pillar includes the design principles 'democratize advanced technologies' and 'experiment more often'?
questions.explanation: Performance Efficiency encourages using managed advanced technologies and experimenting with different configurations to use resources efficiently.

questions.prompt: A team deploys application updates as frequent, small, reversible changes so failures are easy to roll back. Which Well-Architected pillar does this practice support?
questions.explanation: 'Make frequent, small, reversible changes' is a design principle of the Operational Excellence pillar.

questions.prompt: A company tags resources and uses cost reports to attribute spending to each business unit. Which Well-Architected pillar's practices does this follow?
questions.explanation: 'Analyze and attribute expenditure' is a Cost Optimization design principle that helps identify return on investment and reduce waste.

questions.prompt: Under the Well-Architected Sustainability pillar, what is the customer responsible for?
choices: Recycling and disposing of AWS server hardware at the end of its life
Sustainability in the cloud, such as optimizing workloads and resource utilization
Choosing the renewable energy suppliers that power AWS facilities worldwide
Sustainability of the cloud, such as the energy efficiency of AWS data center facilities
questions.explanation: AWS handles sustainability of the cloud (efficient infrastructure); customers handle sustainability in the cloud by designing efficient workloads.

questions.prompt: A security architect wants to reduce the need for direct human access to production data by using tools and automation. Which Security pillar design principle is this?
questions.explanation: 'Keep people away from data' reduces the risk of mishandling and human error; the other options are principles of other pillars.

questions.prompt: What are AWS Well-Architected Lenses?
choices: Monitoring dashboards that score running workloads in real time against benchmarks
Extensions of the framework with guidance for specific industries or technologies
Templates that automatically deploy a reference architecture into an account
Paid consulting engagements delivered by AWS Support engineers on request
questions.explanation: Lenses, such as the Serverless Lens, extend Well-Architected guidance to particular technology or industry domains.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is one of the pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
questions.explanation: The six pillars are Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization and Sustainability.

questions.prompt: Which AWS Cloud Adoption Framework perspective focuses on the confidentiality, integrity and availability of data and cloud workloads?
questions.explanation: The Security perspective helps achieve confidentiality, integrity and availability of data and workloads.

questions.prompt: Which list correctly orders the phases of cloud transformation described in the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework?
questions.explanation: AWS CAF describes an iterative journey of Envision, Align, Launch and Scale.

questions.prompt: In which AWS CAF phase does an organization deliver pilot initiatives into production and demonstrate incremental business value?
questions.explanation: The Launch phase delivers pilots in production; Scale then expands them to the desired size and business impact.

questions.prompt: During cloud adoption, a company identifies capability gaps across the six CAF perspectives and creates an action plan to address stakeholder concerns. Which CAF phase is this?
questions.explanation: The Align phase identifies capability gaps and cross-organizational dependencies and builds an action plan.

questions.prompt: Which business outcome does the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework identify as a benefit of cloud transformation?
choices: Transfer of AWS data center hardware ownership to the customer
Guaranteed elimination of all application downtime and outages
Improved environmental, social and governance (ESG) performance
Removal of all regulatory compliance obligations for the organization
questions.explanation: AWS CAF lists reduced business risk, improved ESG performance, increased revenue and increased operational efficiency as outcomes.

questions.prompt: A company wants a data-driven business case for migration by analyzing its on-premises servers and projecting the cost of running them on AWS. Which service should it use?
questions.explanation: Migration Evaluator collects on-premises usage data and builds a business case; Cost Explorer only analyzes existing AWS spending.

questions.prompt: Which service collects usage, configuration and dependency data about on-premises servers to help plan a migration?
questions.explanation: Application Discovery Service gathers server data and dependencies for planning; Application Migration Service performs the actual rehost.

questions.prompt: A company must exit its data center in six months and move hundreds of applications as fast as possible. Which migration strategy is usually quickest?
questions.explanation: Rehosting moves applications without changes, so it can be done at scale quickly; refactoring takes the most time.

questions.prompt: Which migration strategy typically requires the most time and effort but can deliver the greatest cloud-native benefits?
questions.explanation: Refactoring changes the application's architecture, which is effortful but unlocks scalability and agility benefits.

questions.prompt: Which AWS program provides a migration methodology, tools, training and potential funding to help organizations migrate to AWS?
questions.explanation: MAP is a comprehensive program that includes methodology, tooling, training and investment to accelerate migrations.

questions.prompt: In the AWS Migration Acceleration Program, which phase focuses on building a business case and assessing the organization's readiness?
questions.explanation: MAP has three phases: Assess (readiness and business case), Mobilize (plan and close gaps), and Migrate and Modernize.

questions.prompt: A company wants to run software on Amazon EC2 using licenses it already owns. What is this licensing model called?
questions.explanation: BYOL lets customers use existing eligible licenses on AWS instead of paying for license-included instances.

questions.prompt: Which licensing option includes the cost of the software license in the hourly price of an EC2 instance?
questions.explanation: With license-included instances, such as Windows Server, the license cost is bundled into the instance price.

questions.prompt: How do server costs in a traditional data center usually differ from costs on AWS?
choices: Both are billed by the second based only on actual resource usage
On premises: variable monthly costs; on AWS: fixed annual payments in advance
On premises: large up-front fixed costs; on AWS: variable pay-as-you-go costs
On premises costs include free spare capacity for unexpected peaks
questions.explanation: Data centers require buying capacity in advance, while AWS charges only for what is consumed.

questions.prompt: Which statement best defines cloud computing?
choices: On-demand delivery of IT resources over the internet with pay-as-you-go pricing
Buying hardware from a vendor that installs and maintains it on premises
Running virtual machines only within a company's own private network
Renting a dedicated physical data center under a multi-year fixed-price lease
questions.explanation: AWS defines cloud computing as on-demand delivery of IT resources over the internet with pay-as-you-go pricing.

questions.prompt: Which term describes the likelihood that stored data will not be lost over time?
questions.explanation: Durability measures protection against data loss; availability measures whether data or services can be accessed when needed.

questions.prompt: A web tier places orders into an Amazon SQS queue that a separate processing tier reads from. Which architectural principle does this demonstrate?
questions.explanation: A queue decouples components so each can scale and fail independently.

questions.prompt: Why does using a managed service such as Amazon RDS reduce operational burden compared with self-managing a database on servers?
choices: Managed services remove the need for any access control
The customer no longer needs to design any database schema or tables
AWS handles tasks such as hardware provisioning, patching and backups
AWS takes ownership of the customer's data and its classification
questions.explanation: Managed services offload undifferentiated administration while the customer still owns schemas, data and access.

questions.prompt: Which disaster recovery strategy usually has the lowest cost but the longest recovery time?
questions.explanation: Backup and restore keeps nothing running, so it is cheapest but takes longest to recover.

questions.prompt: A company keeps a replicated database and minimal core services always running in a second Region, scaling out application servers only during a disaster. Which DR strategy is this?
questions.explanation: Pilot light keeps only the core components live; warm standby runs a scaled-down but fully functional copy.

questions.prompt: Which disaster recovery strategy runs a scaled-down but fully functional copy of the production environment that can be scaled up quickly?
questions.explanation: Warm standby keeps a complete, smaller environment running so it can take traffic immediately and scale up.

questions.prompt: Which disaster recovery approach provides the lowest recovery time and data loss but at the highest cost?
questions.explanation: Running full production in multiple sites simultaneously minimizes RTO and RPO but costs the most.

questions.prompt: What does a recovery point objective (RPO) define?
choices: The number of Regions a workload must be deployed across
The maximum acceptable time to restore service after an outage
The percentage of time a service must be available to users
The maximum acceptable amount of data loss, measured in time
questions.explanation: RPO is how much data, in time, can be lost; the time to restore service is the recovery time objective (RTO).

questions.prompt: What does a recovery time objective (RTO) define?
choices: The maximum acceptable time to restore service after an interruption
How frequently backups must be taken to meet internal audit requirements
The time needed to migrate a workload to a different Region
The maximum acceptable amount of data loss, measured in time
questions.explanation: RTO is the maximum acceptable downtime; RPO covers the acceptable data loss window.

questions.prompt: Which benefit does defining infrastructure as code most directly provide?
choices: Physical isolation of resources from all other AWS customers
Automatic compliance with every industry regulation and standard
Elimination of all infrastructure costs for every environment
Repeatable, consistent deployments that can be versioned and reviewed
questions.explanation: Infrastructure as code makes environments reproducible and supports the 'perform operations as code' principle.

questions.prompt: A team writes runbooks, holds post-incident reviews and shares lessons learned to improve procedures. Which Well-Architected pillar does this support?
questions.explanation: 'Learn from all operational events and failures' is part of the Operational Excellence pillar.

questions.prompt: A team monitors service quotas, plans network topology and designs workloads to withstand component failures. Which Well-Architected pillar is it focusing on?
questions.explanation: Foundations such as quotas and network topology plus failure management are Reliability best practice areas.

questions.prompt: Which activity is an example of 'undifferentiated heavy lifting' that AWS can take over?
choices: Deciding which customers to target with new marketing campaigns
Designing the unique product features that set the company apart
Defining the core business rules implemented in an application
Maintaining and replacing physical servers and data center equipment
questions.explanation: Running infrastructure does not differentiate a business; AWS handles it so customers can focus on their products.

questions.prompt: Which deployment model uses virtualization and resource management tools inside a company's own data center, sometimes called a private cloud?
questions.explanation: An on-premises (private cloud) deployment runs cloud-like tooling on the company's own infrastructure.

questions.prompt: A company stops its development EC2 instances every night and weekend. Which cloud economics concept is it taking advantage of?
choices: Volume discounts from long-term Reserved Instances
Paying only for resources while they are running
questions.explanation: With on-demand pricing, stopping unused compute avoids paying for idle capacity.

questions.prompt: After moving all workloads from its data center to AWS, which cost does a company typically NO longer pay directly?
choices: Data center power, cooling and physical security
Licenses for its own proprietary business software
questions.explanation: Facility costs are absorbed by AWS; the company still pays for its people and its own software.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
choices: A contract that guarantees a specific uptime percentage for workloads
A paid certification that every production AWS workload must pass
A service that automatically re-architects applications for the cloud
A set of best practices and questions for evaluating and improving cloud architectures
questions.explanation: The framework provides pillars, design principles and questions to review architectures; it is guidance, not a guarantee.

questions.prompt: Which practice best applies the principle 'stop guessing your capacity needs'?
choices: Ordering hardware a quarter in advance
Buying enough servers for the peak demand expected in five years
Using automatic scaling to match capacity to actual demand
Running all instances at maximum size permanently
questions.explanation: Scaling automatically with demand removes the need to forecast and over-provision capacity.

questions.prompt: Which cost benefit of serverless services such as AWS Lambda is MOST significant for workloads with idle periods?
choices: A fixed monthly fee that does not change with traffic
No charge for idle capacity because you pay per use
Discounts for keeping servers running around the clock
Unlimited free compute for every request processed
questions.explanation: Serverless pricing is based on requests and execution time, so idle time costs nothing.

questions.prompt: Which AWS tool shows the estimated carbon emissions associated with a customer's AWS usage?
questions.explanation: The Customer Carbon Footprint Tool in the Billing console reports estimated emissions from AWS usage.

questions.prompt: Which statement about AWS Availability Zones within a Region is accurate?
choices: They share a single power source and cooling system to reduce overall cost
They are connected to each other only over the public internet
They are located in different countries to provide legal isolation
They are physically separate and linked by low-latency, redundant networking
questions.explanation: AZs are isolated from each other's failures yet connected by fast, redundant private networking for synchronous replication.

questions.prompt: Which type of Reserved Instance allows you to change the instance family, operating system or tenancy during the term?
questions.explanation: Convertible RIs can be exchanged for different attributes; Standard RIs offer a bigger discount but less flexibility.

questions.prompt: Which Reserved Instance payment option provides the largest discount?
questions.explanation: Paying the full amount up front gives the deepest discount compared with partial or no up-front payment.

questions.prompt: A company commits to a consistent amount of usage of a specific instance family, such as M7g, in one Region for one year. Which pricing option fits?
questions.explanation: EC2 Instance Savings Plans give the highest Savings Plan discount in exchange for committing to an instance family in a Region.
